"Noor's ability felt a bit short on multiple fronts, so it is receiving some follow-up changes in order to double down on his shield countering capabilities as well as his survivability. The Horus Lance Launcher will receive multiple improvements to make his ability more reactive, more punishing against ballistic shield operators when they make positioning mistakes, but also more rewarding for the risk Noor takes while equipping the launcher."
HORUS LANCE LAUNCHER
Drilling time reduced on Ballistic Shields, soft surfaces, and solid surfaces (non-destructible surfaces) to 1.5s (from 2s).
Guardbreak strength on projectile impact against ballistic shield operators is increased to 100% (from 30%).
Equipping the Horus Lance Launcher uses Quickdraw animations, equip animation timings are reduced to 0.4s (from 0.9s).
Horus Lance impact damage against an operator is increased to 80 (from 50).
Horus Lance hitbox improvements for better accuracy and consistency.
Horus Lance damages Ballistic shield operators while in the removal animation.

Tachanka's Shumikha Launcher relies on bouncing projectiles to deploy fire. While this allows him to apply pressure without exposing himself to enemy fire, the behavior can be difficult to control in situations requiring precision. Additionally, the delay caused by the bouncing mechanic reduces responsiveness, which can be critical in fast-paced engagements where even small timing differences can determine the outcome of a round.

Therefore, we want to improve usability and responsiveness of the Shumikha Launcher by lowering the skill floor required to use the gadget effectively, while providing players with greater control and adaptability depending on the situation.

Introducing an impact-triggered mode allows Tachanka to respond more effectively in precise or time-sensitive scenarios, improving reliability when targeting specific positions or reacting to enemy movement. At the same time, retaining the bouncing behavior preserves his ability to set up layered denial and control space indirectly. The choice between the 2 modes enables greater adaptability, allowing players to select the most appropriate method based on the situation.
SHUMIKHA LAUNCHER
Added firing mode to trigger Incendiary Grenades on impact.
Solid Snake's Radar provides strong utility across multiple situations, allowing him to apply pressure without much risk.
We want to slightly reduce Snake's overall utility to encourage more deliberate usage and clearer prioritization of targets.
SOLITON RADAR MK III
Precision mode charges: Reduced to 3 (from 4).
We want to improve Valkyrie's ability to set up and leverage her cameras more efficiently, enhancing her ability to create lines of sight without increasing her overall power.
The addition of the Glaive-12 allows her to create lines of sight more quickly and from further.
LOADOUT
Secondary weapons: Added Glaive-12.

Instead, they focus on polishing gameplay details, improving consistency, and enhancing quality-of-life without shifting the meta. We want to improve the responsiveness and reliability of Capitao's fire bolts, ensuring they apply pressure more quickly once deployed.
FIRE BOLT
Expansion: Reduced delay between expansions to 0.9 seconds (from 1).

The Taser only works full power when enemies move toward Clash, while its impact remains significantly low when they run away. This distinction reinforces directional counterplay and encourages players to adapt their positioning during engagements. By increasing the slowdown when enemies retreat we enhance Clash's ability to maintain pressure and control space when enemies attempt to disengage.
TASER

This change allows Osa to place her shield in a wider range of situations, improving flexibility and reducing friction when setting up positions.

We want to reinforce the threat and clarity of fire-based hazards across the game by increasing their lethality, ensuring that standing or crossing these areas carries more immediate consequences.

items.text: Operation System Override took Rainbow Six Siege by storm when it launched on June 2, bringing a major Dokkaebi rework, the new-yet-familiar Calypso Casino map, and a competitive overhaul with Ranked 3.0. Now, halfway through the season, the development team is implementing additional Operator balancing, mouse and keyboard support for consoles, a limited-time event, a Ranked map rotation, and rotating Operator trials.

The fan-favorite limited-time event is back, bringing Siege’s intense tactical gameplay into a fast-paced, 1v1 duel environment. A pure test of your skill, the 1v1 arcade is filled with short, high-intensity matches that focus on gunplay, movement, and gadget skill. Gameplay was designed based on community feedback, and features shorter matches, less downtime, and more variety. Some changes from the last iteration include:
Updated map pool: House has been removed, with Coastline, Consulate, and Outback added. There are 5 total maps (up from 3)
Bomb sites are now automatically revealed
Reduced prep phase duration
Attrition replaces Operator bans – winning players can no longer select the Operator they used in the previous round
Now uses Ranked skill table for matchmaking (instead of Quick Match data)
New players without a Ranked rating will receive an initial skill estimate
The 1v1 arcade is out now and runs for two weeks, so don’t miss a moment of the action!
Several Operators have been slightly rebalanced to help improve fair, competitive gameplay; make them more versatile in gameplay; and help cement their role in an Attacker or Defender lineup.
Dokkaebi
Global cooldown removed
Cooldown is now specific to the target Dokkaebi sent the Jegeo Payload to
Cooldown is now 14 seconds (increased from 7)
Wamai
Reduced Mag-NET activation time from 1.5s to 0.5s for faster projectile interception
Increased Mag-NET charge regeneration rate from 40s to 20s per charge
Added a deployable shield to secondary gadget options
Retained Proximity Alarm as a secondary gadget option, but replaced Impact Grenades with a Nitro Cell (C4)
Total maximum Charges 7 (was 5)
Jäger
Changed to 3 Speed / 1 Armor (from 2 Speed / 2 Armor)
Zofia
Increased KS79 Lifeline Ammunition
Concussion Grenades: 3 (up from 2)
Impact Grenades 3 (up from 2)
Lesion
Reduced GU Mine refill time to 25s (from 30s)
Twitch
Reduced Shock Drone shot recharge time to 28s (from 30s)
Melusi
Increased Banshee area of effect to 4.3m (from 4m)
Rauora
Reduces cooldown between gadget shots to 1s (from 3s)
416-C Carbine
Improvements to vertical recoil, horizontal recoil, & Recoil evolution

Native mouse and keyboard support on consoles is officially here, covering gameplay, UI, and system interactions. Text chat is also available to all members of squads that have mouse and keyboard players for seamless team communication.

To ensure competitive fairness, the game will automatically detect what input you’re using, and mouse and keyboard players will be placed in the PC crossplay matchmaking pool. Mousetrap enforcement remains active for players who attempt to circumvent these matchmaking rules.
A mid-season update means a Ranked map rotation to help keep the competitive experience feel fresh and varied.

[p align="start"]Wamai and Jäger occupy a similar space as projectile denial operators, and our goal is to maintain their shared role while further differentiating their gameplay. Wamai’s ability has always offered more flexibility and reactivity than Jäger’s, but it also requires greater player attention to leverage effectively.

[p align="start"]With this set of changes, we are emphasizing that reactive playstyle by making Mag‑Nets more available and responsive, while also expanding his loadout flexibility. Our intent is to reinforce Wamai as a catcher who rewards higher player input and awareness, allowing him to adapt more effectively throughout the round.
Charge update frequency 20s (was 40s)
Total maximum Charges 7 (was 6).
Reduced activation time to 0.5s (was 1.5s).
Add Deployable Shield.
Replace Impact Grenades with C4.

[p align="start"]A longer per-target cooldown reduces repeated pressure on the same defenders, providing clearer recovery windows. Players who have already been affected gain temporary relief, allowing for repositioning and more meaningful decision-making.

[p align="start"]At the same time, Dokkaebi gains flexibility, as her effectiveness is no longer tied to a single cooldown. This enables more adaptative usage, rewarding awareness of defender positioning and better timing when coordinating pushes.

[p align="start"]The new cooldown system also encourages Dokkaebi to distribute the activations more thoughtfully. Focusing repeatedly on the same target or sending a payload when not ready to capitalize on it becomes less efficient and effective, promoting more strategic target selection.
Cooldown is now per-target (from ability global)
Cooldown: 14 seconds (from 7)
[p align="start"]Alongside the updates to Wamai, we are making targeted adjustments to Jäger to further differentiate their roles as projectile denial operators.

[p align="start"]Jäger will return to a 3 Speed - 1 Health configuration, reinforcing his strength in mobility. Unlike Wamai, Jäger’s utility is more static once deployed, making repositioning and adaptation during the round more limited. Increasing his mobility allows for faster rotations across the map and more efficient deployment during the Preparation Phase.
[p align="start"]Additionally, we are improving the recoil control of the 416‑C to increase its consistency; more details can be found in the Refinement Changes section further down.
Speed: 3 (was 2)
Health: 1 (was 2)

[p align="start"]In Y11S1.3, we began refining Zofia’s kit by improving the recoil of the M762, followed in Y11S2.0 by restoring her 2 Health / 2 Speed configuration to reinforce her mobility and overall reliability in engagements.

[p align="start"]As part of this continued refinement, we are increasing the available ammunition for the KS79 Lifeline, raising both Concussion and Impact Grenades to 3 charges each. This adjustment is intended to give Zofia more flexibility and presence throughout the round, allowing her to apply her utility more consistently while reinforcing her role as a versatile and adaptable attacker.
Concussion Ammunition set to 3 (was 2)
Impact Grenades Ammunition set to 3 (was 2)

[p align="start"]These are small adjustments that don’t aim to alter an operator’s overall power level or flexibility. Instead, they focus on polishing gameplay details, improving consistency, and enhancing quality-of-life without shifting the meta. Our goal is to maintain a steady stream of these refinements alongside major updates, helping the game evolve and improve at a constant pace.
[p align="start"]The 416‑C was historically a very strong weapon, particularly when paired with the higher demand for projectile denial, contributing to Jäger’s popularity on defense.

[p align="start"]As part of the broader adjustments aimed at reinforcing Jäger’s role, we are smoothing the recoil of the 416‑C to improve its consistency, especially in longer‑range engagements. Given that Jäger’s utility is more static and straightforward compared to Wamai’s, this change ensures that his primary weapon remains reliable and accessible.

[p align="start"]Our goal is to support Jäger’s identity as a more straightforward catcher, allowing both experienced players and newcomers to engage effectively without lowering the skill ceiling tied to recoil control.

Thorn has long struggled to secure her role as a reliable trapper. The current Razor Bloom setup often lacks impact during rounds as its effectiveness depends heavily on pre-planting and concealment. If Attackers choose alternate paths, the traps become irrelevant.
This update aims to resolve Thorn’s “bark but no bite” issue by making Razor Bloom Shells more flexible and impactful throughout the round. Key changes include:
Reduced activation time for faster response.
Increased Shells quantity to allow more coverage and reactive placement.
Slightly reduced lethal range in exchange for quicker detection-to-trigger timing.
Added a 15-second survivor penalty that adds bleed and slows movement, similar to Frost's Welcome Mats when self-removed.
These adjustments transform Razor Blooms into a more dynamic and reactive tool, ensuring Thorn remains a meaningful threat beyond the Preparation Phase.
RAZOR BLOOM SHELLS
Trigger time after detection: 1.35s (was 2.9s)
Damage

Max damage zone: 0m-1m from center
Activation time after deployment: 1s (was 5s)
Detection and explosion range: 4m
Slowdown and bleed debuff after being hit: 15s
Starting quantity: 4 (was 3)

The R6 ShieldGuard team is here to highlight the progress made this season, with some news on what's to come.

[p align="start"]Competitive integrity is the foundation of Siege, and we've continued to listen to your concerns, and monitor your feedback. It's clear however, that cheating remains to be a core issue. We're committed to the betterment of Siege for all players, and although we have seen recent, minor improvements, it's important to note that this is part of a larger journey and vision.

[p align="start"]Firstly, we can confirm that we'll be doubling the cadence of R6 ShieldGuard updates in Season 4. Secondly, to help us develop the necessary improvements more quickly, we're working to share technology with partners across the industry. The R6 ShieldGuard team is also continuing to expand to accelerate future updates.

[p align="start"]For multiple seasons now, we've been deploying R6 ShieldGuard updates with each patch and hotfix, but in Season 4 this will be changing. Starting next season, we'll be doubling how often these R6 ShieldGuard updates are pushed to the game, disrupting cheat makers more than ever before.

[p align="start"]Our team has targeted high profile cheat makers, and we are seeing results with these efforts. After recent updates were made, R6 ShieldGuard perma banned 1500 cheaters using high profile cheats, with an additional 2000 cheaters being perma banned while using a single notorious cheat product.

[p align="start"]This season, we've been working to increase the impact we're having on cheat makers, keeping them offline for longer, and we've started to have more success in this area. This has resulted in us keeping select cheats offline for up to 5-7 days, up from 1 or 2 days previously. Our target is to carry this momentum forward, while we work to address the cheats that are disrupting legitimate players.

[p align="start"]ELO trapping is the act of intentionally matchmaking against known opponents who deliberately throw games to secure unfair wins and boost another account's ranking. A ban wave targeting ELO trappers was completed in October, with over 4300 cheaters being perma banned (including 36% of the top 100 console players). We will continuously ban any accounts related to ELO trapping.

[p align="start"]This season we've seen bots infiltrating our less competitive game modes, mainly Team Deathmatch. We've perma banned over 6000 bots this season, and any accounts with suspicious botting activity will continue to be perma banned.

[p align="start"]We've talked about our anti-recoil detection efforts before, and we want to confirm that it continues to be developed as part of R6 ShieldGuard. This is a complex, machine learning system which needs to train using high volumes of data. The system is currently in its data gathering phase behind the scenes, with further development and testing stages to follow.

[p align="start"]Here are our updated perma ban figures covering the last 12 months, with new data for August, September and October. The total monthly perma bans issued has continued to increase from February, with ban waves being completed across multiple cheat types.

We've been reading your feedback and recognize there are important subjects we need to address.

We acknowledge that we haven't communicated clearly enough about what we've been working on since the launch of Siege X, and we understand the frustration that's caused. We're committed to improving transparency and taking meaningful action on the issues you've raised. Based on your feedback, our upcoming priorities include anti-cheat, balancing, and ranked improvements. You can read about the current status of each below, with more updates coming on the road to Munich Major in November. We want to thank you all for your continued support while we work through these challenges, it means a lot.
[p align="start"]- Alex Karpazis and Joshua Mills, on behalf of the Siege team

[p align="start"]Our systems in Siege X did not keep pace with the surge of cheaters that followed the move to Free Access, though we have made some progress. This is a difficult topic to address without tipping off cheat makers to our next move, so without saying too much here are a few key areas the team is working to improve, backed by additional resources.
Target high profile cheat makers and the use of a single notorious cheat product through advancements in Cheat Detection.
Disrupt marketplace exploits.
Issue permanent bans to players caught using these exploits.

[p align="start"]We've heard that updates can feel like all nerfs, no buffs, so we're changing up our approach when unexpected metas form and will prioritize a fun experience. We have high ambitions for larger system changes for the game's balancing, which will go into testing soon.
In patch 3.3 (coming Oct 14) we'll be reverting Denari's nerf. We reacted a little too quickly on tuning him based on what we saw on the test server. Additionally, Denari's Glaive-12 will be buffed.
Solis will be receiving her impact grenades back to make her more fun to play. We can still see her influence in matches and how players use her shotgun for those post-plant situations.
For Y10S4, we can confirm that Thermite, Hibana and Maverick will all be receiving buffs. Ace will have a lot more competition!

Y10S4 will also introduce the Testing Grounds, a place to help us gather initial feedback and test implementation of gameplay features before they're integrated. An Armor and Speed system change for operators will be our first Testing Grounds subject.
[p align="start"]Ranked 2.0 hasn't hit the mark yet and we're working on major changes. There will be matchmaking updates to start in Season 4 with more meaningful updates on the way.
With Y10S4, matchmaking will get more specific with Rank and squad size factored in.
We are actively developing what we call Ranked Overhaul, with the objective of offering visible Ranked Reward Progression, as well as a visible Skill Progression.
Player consultations are in progress with this new system, and we'll be running workshops during the Munich Major to further refine the design.
We aim to have the Ranked Overhaul live in the first half of year 11.

[p align="start"]With much of this year's focus on setting a new foundation for updates to come, recent seasonal content has understandably felt lighter, especially for veteran players. We are looking at adjusting our seasonal approach to bring more substance to mid-season updates and we will share more on this topic during the November Munich Major.

[p align="start"]This update isn't exhaustive, but expect to hear more from us, and please continue sharing your reports, feedback, survey responses and gameplay. Your passion and commitment keep Siege growing. Your priorities are our priorities, and together we'll keep building Siege into the best it can be.
[p align="start"]We look forward to celebrating our tenth anniversary together!
[p align="start"]{-}7
[p align="start"]The Siege Team

The R6 ShieldGuard team is here to give an update on Anti-Cheat in Siege X. Today we'll look at the status since the release of Siege X and R6 ShieldGuard, and cover what's coming in the future. Check out the team's plans below.

[p align="start"]Since the launch of Siege X, it's clear that there has been a surge in cheater reports. The share of matches featuring players who receive 4 or more cheater reports within that single game has risen from an average of 1.8% to 2.5%. This spike is tied to the evolution of in-game exploits and the ongoing development of cheat programs. We know the impact that this has had on the enjoyment of the game for many and we are very actively working on solutions.

[p align="start"]We've deployed several fixes since launch, though some of the improvements needed to strengthen R6 ShieldGuard will require longer-term development. Our goal is to make meaningful progress throughout Season 3 and beyond, ensuring we protect the game's integrity and improve your overall experience.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/8328525/dc268c9ab0d8117bdd738440dd1256fcad12e550.jpg"]

[p align="start"]With the release of Siege X and the increased number of players, bugs were found in the game that could be used to gain an unfair advantage over other teams and players. These exploits are also a form of cheating.

[p align="start"]With the help of our community, we've been able to address several major exploits as part of our most recent patches, including multiple teleportation glitches, legitimate external overlay applications providing an unfair visual advantage, impossible defusing spots or impossible use of weapons and gadgets, and crashes caused by specific operators. We have also identified and are actively fixing additional issues, with updates rolling out as soon as they're ready.

[p align="start"]We want to sincerely thank everyone who has contributed - content creators, players, and those who have submitted reports via R6Fix. Your input has been crucial in helping us reproduce and resolve many of these exploits. To further prevent new exploits, we're working on a global solution that includes stricter tolerances in given situations to prevent similar exploits. We continue to monitor the situation closely.

[p align="start"]Throughout Operation Daybreak, we have deployed several updates to our underlying in-house obfuscation technology which hides and protects game code. These updates are strengthening our defenses, and while we're already seeing some positive trends, more updates will be coming with every patch and hotfix. We're also constantly investing in reducing and stopping new gameplay violations, while improving our detections, targeting specific cheat features and providers.

[p align="start"]You may have noticed that Siege X occasionally requires a game restart and update. This is part of a new prevention system which has strengthened our anti-cheat defenses overall. While the system has been effective, we've identified bugs that have caused some players to be disconnected from matches or unable to reconnect. We understand how frustrating this can be and sincerely apologize for the disruption. Our team is actively working to resolve these issues so that players can benefit from enhanced protection without any unintended side effects.

[p align="start"]We're actively developing new tools that detect accounts linked to previously banned cheaters. If a banned player attempts to return, they're flagged and removed as soon as suspicious behavior is detected. In addition, we're working on systems to hold players accountable if they knowingly squad up with cheaters. This is part of our broader effort to protect the integrity of the game at every level.

[p align="start"]Check out the last 12 months of perma-ban data, including new data for April to July. We can see here that the number of monthly bans has remained steady since the launch of Operation Prep Phase, with over 11,000 permanent bans issued on average per month. With a rise in cheaters being felt during the month of July however, investigation were started into whether our systems were still banning with the same effectiveness as previous months. This investigation led to adjustments being made to R6 ShieldGuard, which resulted in an additional ban wave being completed in early August.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/8328525/efe9ddce16babb4e73a9753a1cdbcb71037d894f.jpg"]

[p align="start"]Keeping your account secure helps keep the game fair for everyone. That's why we strongly recommend enabling Two-Factor Authentication (2FA), especially using a mobile authenticator app if possible. By turning on 2FA, you're not just protecting your progress, you're helping us to fight cheating and keep the community safe. For more information on 2FA, check our self-help article.
[p align="start"]In-game reporting continues to be the best way to get your reports to us, helping us to identify potential cheaters and take action.
Feeding our automated systems while combining with additional information.

[p align="start"]Protecting the game from cheaters and exploit abusers remains one of our top priorities.

[p align="start"]Throughout July, the team has consistently delivered fixes and improvements. In order to release stable solutions, some of the fixes may take more time, but our commitment to act quickly and effectively when issues arise continues. Elements of our future R6 ShieldGuard updates are also already underway, with more to be revealed soon.
[p align="start"]We're not slowing down. Our focus is clear: keep Siege X fair, secure, and fun for everyone.

The Anti-Toxicity team is here to share a look at how the Reputation System has been performing in the time since its full rollout. Right now, the system is helping to shape a healthier, more respectful Siege experience and in this update, we'll share highlights on key features, ongoing improvements, and what's next.

[p align="start"]The Reputation System was released from Beta in Y10S1, and this means that we now have more data than ever on its impact on players. Since its full activation, the amount of Dishonorable and Disruptive players has dropped by 81% and 54% respectively. Conversely, the number of players in Exemplary has increased by 114% with Esteemed increasing by 45%. It's clear that players have been adapting their behavior and rising to higher Reputation Standings, in turn making the game better for everyone.
[p align="start"]STANDINGS - Y9S4 to Y10S2
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/8328525/895ca5e07824be9872a390aad1871ad46bd56f3b.jpg"]

[p align="start"]Our Anti-Toxicity systems are scaling with Siege X and continue to protect players from disruptive behaviors. We are now seeing a reduction of communication reports per match, with a -14% for Textchat and -27% for Voice Chat. This is also partly thanks to the new Chat Wheel, which allows players to communicate quickly and easily without friction. We can see below that exposure to negative actions dropped significantly with the release of Siege X.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/8328525/08332fb7c310a9a37c791a69535810f8facf38cf.jpg"]

[p align="start"]Since March 2025, we have temporarily banned over 4600 players who had completed an excessive amount of negative actions, accruing a critical number of negative Reputation Units. We can share that these temporary bans have worked well however, with 3 of 5 players adapting their behavior and not going on to offend again.

[p align="start"]The Reputation System is now active in Dual Front and positive and negative actions completed in this mode now impact your Reputation. Dual Front initially released without integration into the Reputation System, though thanks to your feedback, we were able to adapt our plans and bring the activation forward.

[p align="start"]Textchat Moderation went live in December 2024, and since then we've worked to ensure the feature evolved with player feedback. The system is now working well, though we are aware that false detections can sometimes occur, often due to lack of context in a conversation.

[p align="start"]From Y10S3 we will be implementing functionality which will enable players with a Reputation Standing of Respectable and above to report detections which they believe to be incorrectly flagged. This, as well as our ongoing behind-the-scenes updates, will help to fine tune the system, reducing the chances of your messages being falsely flagged.

[p align="start"]In Y10S3 we will be introducing the next step of chat moderation in Siege in the form of Voice Chat moderation. With this addition, players flagged by the system will receive a warning and be subsequently muted if flagged again. In more extreme cases, offenders may find themselves being muted immediately and without warning. In all cases, any flags will carry a Reputation Standing impact, though as with Textchat, players with a positive standing will be able to report false voice communication flags.

[p align="start"]We'll be utilising our experience with the Text Chat Moderation feature to bring balance to this new system. And, as we did with Text Chat Moderation, we'll be giving this feature close attention, ensuring that any false flags can be learned from with changes made to the system quickly.

[p align="start"]Abandonment penalties, although necessary, can be a source of great frustration for those who receive them unfairly. This season we've already lessened the length of penalties, though there is more to come. We are actively working to implement a system that will target repetitive patterns over a longer period and subsequently enable us to reduce frustration for others.

[p align="start"]Privacy Mode is making its way to console in Y10S3. With this release, we'll be making some important updates to Privacy Mode across all platforms. Starting next season, nicknames will be auto assigned, removing the possibility of bad actors creating toxic usernames.All players will also have their nicknames removed at the end of a match, revealing their true usernames.

[p align="start"]We are very proud of the evolution that we’ve made with your feedback, together fostering a more positive environment. The Reputation System is working well in Siege X, helping to protect new and current players. We are devoted to our goal of making Siege a fun and safe game for everyone, and our work will continue through Y10S3 and beyond.
[p align="start"]Your feedback and support will always be key. Stay positive and let’s continue to make the game better!

Today our R6 Shieldguard and Anti-Toxicity teams will be sharing their latest updates. We’ll have a deep dive on features and results from Y10S1, as well as a look at some of the updates coming to the game in the future.

Cheater reports have seen a downward trend throughout Y9S3, and this continued right up to the release of Y10S1.1. Since the Y10S1.1 update, we have seen an increase in cheater reports on PC. Thanks to your in-game cheater reports, our team has identified a correlation to some of our recent security updates. Below we’ll dive into those updates and the action we’re taking to turn this latest development around.

notes.title: MAKING OUR CODE STRONGER – NEW TECHNOLOGY

items.text: In Y10S1 and in partnership with the security teams of Ubisoft, we introduced a hardening technology which enables new ways to secure our game code, making it more robust against cheat makers. This new technology now serves as a foundation for many other security improvements that will ship throughout the year.

The in-game impact of this technology was positive initially, though following Y10S1.1, we recorded an increase in cheater reports. We’ve seen that there is room for improvement, however this has only bolstered our commitment, and so we’ve worked to push new features throughout Y10S1, making the system more secure. Additionally, we’ve kept to our commitment to push security updates alongside patches, and so security hotfixes will continue leading up to and after the release of Siege X. Two additional security hotfixes are scheduled for deployment in May to further reinforce this approach.

notes.title: FIGHTING LAG ABUSE TO PROTECT FAIR PLAY

items.text: In Y10S1, and with the help of the community, we fixed several exploits that were abusing network lag. We want to take the opportunity to heartfully thank the community, from content creators to everyone who submitted R6Fix reports. You have all helped us to both reproduce and fix many of these exploits that were possible on console. We’re continuing to monitor the situation and to help prevent lag exploits on a wider basis, we are currently working on a global solution, using stricter network tolerations (More info to come soon).

Previously we shared that console cheater reports increased after the launch of Crossplay, and that we fixed an exploit that would allow spoofers to by-pass detection. We can now confirm that reports have seen a drop of approximately 20%. However, Console cheater reports are still higher than pre-crossplay numbers and we are aware of anti-recoil cheats disrupting the community. Although our data shows that MouseTrap is performing well, catching spoofing devices such as Xim and Cronus, it currently lacks anti-recoil detection capabilities. We want to be clear, anti-recoil cheats are not acceptable, irrespective of platform. Although we cannot communicate on our roadmap at this time, rest assured that this is one of the R6 Shieldguard team’s top priorities, and we are actively researching solutions. In the meantime, please continue to submit in-game reports.

We will keep making our code stronger with Siege X and beyond. A security update will go live at launch, with more updates rolling out season after season specifically targeting the ability for cheats to stay online and disrupt the game.

notes.title: R6 SHIELDGUARD UPDATES LIVE, NO MAINTENANCE REQUIRED

items.text: A major update to R6 Shieldguard will allow us to distribute new executables with updated security measures to players without the need for scheduled maintenance. Periodically, a security update will be downloaded, and players will be asked to reboot their game. Note that this will never happen during a match. After a reboot, players can continue playing, knowing that they are now on a newer executable with new security measures. This will make cheats more difficult to make and more costly to maintain, forcing cheats to stay offline longer.

Thanks to the new gameplay violations introduced in Y10S1, combined with automated data analysis and investigations from our team, we continued the momentum from the start of the year by issuing strong permanent ban waves in March, resulting in over 6,500 R6 Shieldguard perma-bans that month alone. On average since the beginning of the year, R6 Shieldguard has issued about 2 times more permanent bans than last year, a clear testament to the performance and evolution of our systems.
Check out the last 12 months of perma-ban data, including new data for 2025.

With Siege X on the horizon, R6 Shieldguard remains at the forefront of the fight against cheating. Our team is actively researching, developing, and evolving across all areas of the Anti-Cheat space. Whether you’re playing on PC or Console, we have exciting plans to further enhance your experience and ensure a fair game for everyone.

Operation Prep Phase marked the full release of the Reputation System; the Beta tag is gone, and Impacts are now online. This is the first time that players have seen rewards or repercussions based on their Reputation Standing alone, and today our Anti-Toxicity team will be detailing how Impacts have affected the game so far. The team will also be sharing a few details on upcoming updates, and how they plan to make Siege and its Anti-Toxicity systems better for everyone.

The activation of Impacts has resulted in a positive change in player behavior, and we’ve got the data to show it. The percentage of players in positive Standings (Respectable, Esteemed, Exemplary) has increased across the board, while the percentage of those in negative Standings (Disruptive and Dishonorable) has reduced. We can see that players who were previously recurrently toxic have adapted to the new Impacts by changing their behavior. We’d also like to insist on the fact that “Respectable” is a good standing where players receive positive perks.

notes.title: In comparison to last season we have seen

items.text: A decrease of -23% players in Dishonorable.
An increase of +37% players in Exemplary.

There are a number of in-game behaviors that have seen an improvement as part of the shift in Standing distribution. Here are a few stats showing just how behavior has changed in Y10S1 thanks to the full release of the Reputation System.
-21% change to the number of negative actions per player match (see graph below).
+21% change to the number of positive actions per player match (see graph below).
-22% intentional team kills in Ranked and -23% in Standard.
-16% abandoned matches in Ranked, and -14% in Standard.
-35% friendly gadget destruction in Ranked, and -43% in Standard.

Here is a detailed look at the amount of negative actions completed per player match, where we can see an overall downward trend. Of course, we do expect these figures to evolve over time, and particularly within the first 90 days of Impact activation. Our team will continue to analyze this data as we move forward, reacting and adapting where necessary.

This season, we added additional measures specifically targeting consistently toxic players. Dishonorable players who continue to significantly exceed the negative unit limit are now automatically temporarily banned. If those players continue to be disruptive after their return, they are manually reviewed for potential permanent ban.
Looking ahead, we have plans to improve the Reputation System experience. Our plans include:
Introducing more nuanced team-kill tracking to alleviate frustration around unintentional incidents.
Enhancing and expanding positive action recognition.
Addressing new areas of concern that hinder a positive environment, such as in-game idling, boosting with cheaters, and more.

Our Automated Textchat Moderation is helping to reduce toxicity in the game. The percentage of removed and flagged messages has decreased by 50% since launch, even while more messages are being sent overall (see graph below). Over 200 million text chat messages are analyzed each month and fewer than 1% of these are being removed, with less than 2% being flagged.

We are continuously fine-tuning the system to minimize false positives as much as possible (any messages which are flagged or removed unnecessarily). Currently, false positives are estimated to make up 0.1% of all flagged or removed messages, equating to around 6,000 messages per month. We know that an incorrect flag feels unfair; rest assured that a single false positive should not severely impact your Reputation Standing. We rely on your help to improve the system by reporting any incorrect detections that you experience through R6Fix. Thanks for your cooperation!
While the Reputation System has our full and ongoing support, our team is also working on more features to improve the overall game experience, player comfort, and privacy.
Enhancing detection and enforcement to address the most toxic players using in-game voice chat, across both PC and consoles.

notes.title: Improved Privacy Settings for PC and Consoles

items.text: Automatically assigning nicknames to players.
Enabling all privacy settings on consoles.
Reducing frustration caused by “unfair” abandonment penalties due to crashes.
Refining detection to focus on players who frequently abandon matches on a long window period.
Introducing greater granularity to reporting options.
Providing players with clearer insights into how their reports are utilized.

We're pleased with the progress made in Siege this year when it comes to reducing toxicity and creating a more welcoming ecosystem. That said, we recognize there is still significant room for growth and refinement. Our ongoing challenge remains to be fostering a positive environment while staying true to the game's unique culture. We do understand that the perception of toxicity can vary greatly though, depending on an individual’s sensitivities. As such, not everyone may align with our standards, which is why your feedback is invaluable to us—we're always listening and evolving.
Thank you for your continued support, understanding, and patience. Stay positive and make the game better!

In Operation Collision Point, we've brought changes to improve the experience for both PC and console players, with continued binary hardening improvements for PC, the new MouseTrap penalty for consoles, and more. Today, our Anti-Cheat team will cover how we got here and what they've been working on, while sharing new data and analytics.

We've touched on this before, but we'd like to share a little more on this here. Late last year, one of the most prevalent cheat vendors exited the Siege space. Leading up to this, the cheat vendor was either offline or being detected, meaning their cheats would be non-functional or result in a ban. This came from our multi-faceted approach to anti-cheat, combining measures in both detection and hardening. This has been a great success for Siege, and our mission is to continue making Siege less viable for cheat vendors.
PC CHEATER REPORTS

Cheater reports have been decreasing, and we've got all-new data to share on this. In the graph above, we can see that cheater reports have been consistently trending downward since the beginning of October, revealing that players are noticing the change in cheater presence. Cheater reports have now decreased by over 40% when compared to our highs of summer 2024, and year on year we've seen a drop upwards of 30%.
CONSOLE CHEATER REPORTS

Console cheater reports have remained largely stable throughout the year. Reports did see an increase at the start of December, though we believe the majority of these are due to the crossplay default setting bug that players had experienced at the launch of Y9S4. We remain focused on our console Anti-Cheat efforts, with more details on MouseTrap below.

notes.title: FUTURE UPDATES - OUR MISSION IS UNCHANGED

items.text: The fight is not over. We know that other cheat makers will attempt to take advantage of the space left behind by a cheat vendor that has pulled out. The removal of this cheat creator changes very little for the Anti-Cheat team roadmap: we will keep investing and innovating in new hardening and detection technologies, to the betterment of Siege.

notes.title: MOUSETRAP - MOUSE & KEYBOARD DETECTION ON CONSOLE

items.text: Reminder: MouseTrap is our console Anti-Cheat which works to detect devices that enable the use of mouse and keyboard.

Y9S4 saw the release of the new MouseTrap penalty system. If detected 3 times, spoofers are forced into the PC matchmaking pool with PC recoil enabled for 90 days. This is a stark change in severity compared to the previous system, which would reduce its effects as soon as the player stopped using a spoofing device. Such a change was made possible by updates to the AI model which reinforced accuracy and further diminished false positives.

Looking at the season launch we know that console players may not have felt the full impact of MouseTrap (as shown in the graph above with a rise in cheater reports at the start of December), with a bug enabling Console to PC crossplay by default, resulting in controller players being unknowingly matched with PC players who were legitimately using keyboard and mouse.

Overall, our data shows that the system is working as expected, detecting and applying penalties to spoofing device users, forcing them into the PC pool. We are confident in our detection, though we know that some players have been able to bypass detection this season. This bypass method is currently being investigated, and we'll be enabling a fix for this soon.

We are closely monitoring MouseTrap and will continue to do so as we ramp up its AI capabilities. Our team is looking into improvements and new ways to utilize AI, which will help us to bolster our detection of cheating on console.

Reminder: Gameplay Violations are actions that are technically possible within the game engine but are in effect forbidden and not possible from a gameplay perspective, such as shooting while sprinting.

Y9S3 has been our best season yet against rage cheating, thanks to a new system we implemented which detects Gameplay Violations. This new system has rendered the use of rage cheats a guaranteed ban, and at its peak, even outperformed our Data Ban system. With this foundational tech in place, it is now easier for the team to implement new Gameplay Violations as rage cheats arise.

We noticed a rise in new lag-based exploits at the beginning of Y9S4. These exploits, which can happen on console, abuse client-server synchronization using network lag. Our team has recently pushed a fix to address these exploits, with an accompanying ban wave. We'd also like to thank players and creators for their help here, as reports submitted via R6Fix played a major role in our initial fixes. We'll continue to monitor this space closely.

Reminder: Binary hardening is the act of using encryption and hardening techniques to update the game code base and enhance security, and we've continued to deploy these updates to the game with each patch.

In Y9S4, we reinforced our hardening capacity even further, with more experts within the team working on improving game security. We've seen success from these efforts, with each patch this season resulting in a decrease in cheater reports and online mentions of cheats on patch day. As well as this, we can share that we're tracking another major cheat provider which has been offline since updates were deployed earlier this season. While we cannot delve into the details of each of our updates, we can confirm that they're delivering concrete results with increased offline time for cheat providers. We hope that you're feeling these results in-game too and as always, these efforts will continue.

We had made the decision to hold Cheater Match Cancellation from the Y9S4 launch, so that additional time could be taken to ensure a smooth release. It's now live, having been activated in an update earlier this season. This has enabled cheaters to be kicked from a match as soon as a ban is issued, at which point the Cheater Match Cancellation feature will be triggered, cancelling the ongoing match for everyone. The result here is a reduction of player time being spent in unfair or illegitimate matches.
Reminder: Botting refers to the use of automated programs designed to perform in-game actions without the interaction of a player.

Our botting detection has been working well, though as we've heard from our community, the temporary bans which were being applied were not enough. With this in mind, we recently changed bans for botting to a permanent ban on the first offence. This change was made possible thanks to improvements in our detection system, leading to greater accuracy and system confidence.

items.text: AUGUST, SEPTEMBER, & OCTOBER - R6 BANS [Data Bans, Gameplay Violation Bans, & more]
R6 Bans performed very well during these months. This was due to our implementation of Gameplay Violations detections, resulting in an uplift in bans for this period.
OCTOBER & NOVEMBER - BATTLEYE BANS

BattlEye bans saw an increase in October and a secondary sharper increase in November. This was a direct result of our increased collaboration with BattlEye, and their own efforts to find new ways of detecting cheats.
DECEMBER

December marked our latest season release, and while we see a decline in overall bans here, we also see that players have reported fewer cheaters compared to previous months (see Cheater Reports Trends above).
As of today, many cheats in the current landscape are either offline, having issues, or being detected by BattlEye.

As you can see from what we've shared today, we've got a multi-pronged approach to Siege Anti-Cheat, and we've seen results over Y9S3 and Y9S4. We will keep pushing and bringing information to you as we move forward.

Y9S4 saw the release of some of our biggest initiatives in Anti-Toxicity with Automated Text Chat Moderation and the Reputation System Refresh. Let's dig into these with our Anti-Toxicity team and see how they've impacted the game and players so far.

The Reputation System Refresh is here, and so far this season, its performance and impact has matched our core pillars (transparency, understandability, and clarity) and expectations. We're finding that players who are regularly or highly toxic are correctly being classified as Dishonorable or Disruptive, while positive players and those who are adapting their behavior are having that reflected with the higher Standings of Respectable, Esteemed, and Exemplary.

Here we have a visual breakdown of the Standings distribution for Y9S4. Currently 1.21% of players are in the Dishonorable (lowest) bracket, with 2.58% being Disruptive (second lowest), and our points system is ensuring that it takes a number of consistent negative steps to get into these brackets. Avoiding negative behavior will help any player to attain the Respectable Standing, and being positive in our matches without negativity, will help you climb higher.

We've seen feedback that it feels too difficult to attain the Exemplary standing and that only a small number of negative actions are needed before dropping out of it. This is by design, so behaviour in this Standing must be close to perfect.

Of course, we will continue to monitor player feedback ensuring that the system works as expected. We are confidently moving towards activating the Reputation System Impacts soon (impacts based on your Reputation Standing) and moving out of Beta.

To start with, we're happy with the introduction of automated text chat moderation in Siege. We know that we got some of the detections wrong, though we've built this system with responsive adaptability in mind, so we have been able to fix issues reported to us within the same day. Below are some examples of messages that were flagged in the early stages of release, that have since been resolved.
"very well shot, masterful aim and play"
"ping4"
"put a mira"
"meastro down"
"toxic"
"emp"
"I shot at lion through the hatch"

We know that in some cases players may come across examples of messages that should or shouldn't be flagged. We are constantly looking at player feedback to refine the system, and are using your reports to apply prompt fixes, improving the experience for everyone.
We've also resolved a bug where some normal messages could be removed if they were sent too quickly in a row, such as "GG" - this was fixed during the hotfix on December 18th.

Since the launch of our automated moderation, we've seen the probability of seeing a player reported for abusive text chat drop by 33% overall, and alongside this, the amount of highly toxic players in text chat has been reduced by 80%.

These figures show that the Automated Text Chat Moderation has had an instant effect on how some players choose to communicate in-game, leading to a more positive experience overall. We will maintain our live balancing ensuring that we can continue protecting players from recurrent or high toxicity.

We are aware that some toxicity remains in-game through the use of offensive Privacy Mode usernames. We are currently working to improve our Anti-Toxicity username solution, and we can confirm that using such usernames may result in a ban. We're constantly banning players who choose to go over the limit with their chosen Privacy Mode usernames.
We want to keep you up to date with some of the other features and improvements that will be coming in the future. Here's a rundown on some topics we're working on in the background:
Automated Voice Chat Moderation
Improving privacy settings for PC and Consoles
Reworking in-game reports: Adding more granularity and improving the feedback loop
Improving the abandonment penalty system

The Reputation System Refresh has seen a successful release that has clearly affected the negative communication in-game. The Automated Text Chat Moderation is also working well, and while we're aware that balancing will always be needed, we're ensuring that we can remain reactive to bring change quickly. Our goal now is to work on bringing the Impacts portion of the Reputation System live, so that players can be recognised for their positivity, or helped towards rehabilitation with impacts on their usual in-game rewards.
